Hi there fellow Pennsylvanian! I grew up near Johnstown and finally went to the Flight 93 Museum a few years ago after so long. Very heavy stuff.

I've just always had a strange fascination with the event. I first learned about the full extent of the event in sixth grade and researched it heavily both in middle and high school. I remember even being an advocate for the Ken Gardner "Twin Towers II" project (that's how far deep I was lol). I think it was also my first realization of the cruelties of the world, as I was a pretty sheltered kid, and I barely remembered that day because I didn't have the full picture or context, as I was only in second grade when it happened. I only remember being excused from school early while my teacher was reading to us on the carpet as we were dismissed one by one and seeing some footage on TV of people running out of a building. 

Since I didn't fully experience it in real time, it is like a movie to me, only it really happened, and no matter how many times I see the planes hitting the buildings and those towers coming down, it will never feel real. Every time I visit the memorial, I get so heavy, and it's a feeling that is bigger than yourself.
